questions.title: Data protection and verification
questions.text: A company stores commercially important information, which should be available to a limited number of management staff only.

parts.title: Data protection and verification (a)
parts.text: Give two measures that the company can take to protect confidential data from being stolen.

scheme.mark_scheme:
Any two from:
- Encrypting data (1)
- Granting limited access rights (1)
- Blocking access from certain locations (1)
- keeping logs of user entries to the system (1)
[max 2]

points.criterion: keeping logs of user entries to the system

scheme.model_answer:
1. Encrypting data
2. Granting limited access rights
scheme.ai_instructions: Award any two valid measures from the mark scheme, max 2.

parts.title: Data protection and verification (b)
parts.text:
One of the data protection methods is data verification.

Define the term data verification.

scheme.mark_scheme:
The computer ensures … (1)
… that data input matches data collected (1)
Done by double entry/on-screen techniques … (1)
…to check if matches (1)
[Max 2]

points.criterion: The computer ensures that data input matches data collected

scheme.model_answer: Data verification is when the computer ensures that the data input matches the data collected, for example by using double entry or on-screen checking to see if the entries match.
scheme.ai_instructions: Max 2. Award credit for defining verification as checking that data has been copied/input accurately, not for validation.

parts.title: Software types and choices (a)(i)
parts.text:
Software can be open-source or closed-source.

Describe open-source software.

scheme.mark_scheme:
- that is released under a Software License that… (1)
…permits each recipient of the software to copy and modify the software; (1)
- does not require recipients to pay a fee or royalty … (1)
… for the permission to copy, modify, or distribute the software. (1)
[Max 2]

points.criterion: Permits each recipient of the software to copy and modify the software
Does not require recipients to pay a fee or royalty
Permission to copy, modify, or distribute the software

scheme.model_answer: Open-source software is released under a software licence that permits recipients to copy, modify and distribute the software without paying a fee or royalty.

parts.title: Software types and choices (a)(ii)
parts.text: Give two advantages of closed-source software over open-source software.

scheme.mark_scheme:
- Range of functionality (1)
- Security (as source code is protected) (1)
- Customer support (1)
- Regular updates (1)
- Troubleshooting available (1)
[Max 2]

points.criterion: Security because source code is protected

scheme.model_answer:

2. Regular updates

parts.title: Software types and choices (b)(i)
parts.text:
A store wants to digitalise its daily purchasing and selling details to make it easier to control them.

Give one reason the store should buy general purpose software in this case.

- Only contains the functions required by the company (1)
- The company will retain the license for the software (1)
- Software can be adapted without permissions from a third party (1)

points.criterion: Only contains the functions required by the company
The company will retain the license for the software
Software can be adapted without permissions from a third party

questions.title: Operating systems and virtual machines
questions.text: A student uses his tablet for drawing. The tablet has an operating system.

parts.title: Operating systems and virtual machines (a)
parts.text: Describe the tasks performed by the operating system to manage the main memory in the tablet.

scheme.mark_scheme:
Reads/writes data to/from RAM (1)
e.g., current data/instructions, from an app so the CPU can access it (1)

Allocates virtual memory, (1)
when there is insufficient RAM to run a program/game (1)

Allocates RAM to optimise performance (1)
Paging / Segmentation (1)

[3]

points.criterion: Gives example such as current data/instructions from an app so the CPU can access it
Explains this is when there is insufficient RAM to run a program/game

scheme.model_answer: The operating system reads and writes current app data and instructions to and from RAM so the CPU can access them. It allocates RAM to programs to optimise performance and can use paging or segmentation. It can also allocate virtual memory when there is insufficient RAM to run a program.
scheme.ai_instructions: Award up to 3 marks from the listed points.

parts.title: Operating systems and virtual machines (b)
parts.text:
A system administrator controls a server using a command line interface.

State one advantage and one disadvantage of using a command line interface for managing the server work.

scheme.mark_scheme:
Advantages:
The server does not need to have a complex operating system and so does not use unnecessary computing resources (1)
Can run complex commands quickly (1)
Server not need to run a graphical user interface (1)

Disadvantages:
Difficult for novices to control. (1)
Need to know the commands first (1)
Easy to make mistakes e.g. typing errors (1)

[Max 2]
Further Information: 1 mark for advantages; 1 mark for disadvantages
scheme.model_answer:
advantage: Can run complex commands quickly.
disadvantage: Need to know the commands first.
scheme.ai_instructions: Award 1 mark for an advantage and 1 mark for a disadvantage. Use the examples in the mark scheme.

parts.title: Operating systems and virtual machines (c)
parts.text:
The system administrator installed a virtual machine.

Explain the difference between hosted and unhosted virtual machines.

scheme.mark_scheme:
A hosted virtual machine is one that runs on top of a host operating system. (1)
An unhosted virtual machine does not require a host operating system. (1)
[2]

points.criterion: A hosted virtual machine is one that runs on top of a host operating system
An unhosted virtual machine does not require a host operating system

scheme.model_answer: A hosted virtual machine runs on top of a host operating system, whereas an unhosted virtual machine does not require a host operating system.

parts.title: CPU buses, architecture and clock speed (d)
parts.text:
When developing a new processor, manufacturers consider different methods to make its performance more efficient.

Describe the effect of increasing the clock speed.

scheme.mark_scheme:
instructions performed more quickly/instructions executed at faster rate (1)
fetch execute cycle will happen faster (1)
increased heat may cause malfunctioning of device // overheating; (1)
[3]
Further Information: Accept calculations/operations/commands for instructions

points.criterion: Instructions performed more quickly/instructions executed at faster rate
Fetch execute cycle will happen faster
Increased heat may cause malfunctioning of device or overheating

scheme.model_answer: Increasing clock speed means instructions are executed at a faster rate and the fetch-execute cycle happens faster. However, it can increase heat and may cause overheating or malfunctioning.

questions.title: Memory and addressing modes

parts.title: Memory and addressing modes (a)
parts.text:

Explain why embedded systems may need RAM.

scheme.mark_scheme:
to store user input. (1)

for example the spin speed and washing program for a washing machine or the time and heat setting on a microwave oven. (1)

User Interface (1)

manage the interaction between the user and the appliance. (1)

parts.title: Memory and addressing modes (b)
parts.text:
Memory addressing in the machine code is performed by the instructions that contain opcode and operand.

Note: opcode ADD adds the operand next to it to the value in the accumulator
operand A is the cell A in the memory (i.e. a variable saved under this name)
operand Index is the value in the Index register to be added to the direct address

Fill in the table below using the letters (A–I) with appropriate definitions and examples of the memory addressing modes. There may be more than one letter in a cell.

A The operand gives the address that stores the value to be used by the instruction

B The operand gives the actual value to be used by the instruction

C ADD A+Index

D ADD A

E The address of the operand is determined by adding the operand to the value stored in the index register.

F ADD #10

G ADD (A)

H ADD 10

I The operand gives the address of a register that stores another address, where the value is located

scheme.mark_scheme:
| Memory addressing mode | Definition | Example |
|---|---|---|
| Immediate Addressing | B | H, F |
| Direct Addressing | A | D |
| Indirect Addressing | I | G |
| Indexed Addressing | E | C |

[9]
Further Information: 1 mark for each letter
scheme.model_answer:
Immediate addressing: Definition B; Example H, F
Direct addressing: Definition A; Example D
Indirect addressing: Definition I; Example G
Indexed addressing: Definition E; Example C

parts.title: Programming languages and reality technologies (c)
parts.text:
Augmented reality and virtual reality technologies are gaining popularity.

Explain the difference between virtual and augmented reality.

scheme.mark_scheme:
A virtual reality replaces your vision, augmented reality adds to it. (1)

VR completely covers and replaces your field of vision, AR apps only show up on your smartphone or tablet screen. (1)
[Max 2]

points.criterion: Virtual reality replaces your vision, augmented reality adds to it

questions.title: Networks, protocols and IP addressing
questions.text: Computer networks are the basis of communication in modern society.

parts.title: Networks, protocols and IP addressing (a)
parts.text:
Domain name is an easy-to-remember representation of an IP address.

Explain how the domain name is used to access a website.

Include the role of Domain Name System (DNS) servers in your explanation.

scheme.mark_scheme:
- A DNS server will contain a list of domain names/ A DNS server will contain a list of corresponding IP addresses (1)

- The browser checks the local (cached) host file to check if it already holds the IP address (1)

- The local (your domain) DNS server is queried for the IP address (1)

- If the local DNS server does not hold the IP address, then the query is passed to another DNS server at a higher level until the IP address is resolved (1)

- The address is passed on to DNS severs lower in the hierarchy (1)

- When the full address has been resolved, the IP address is then passed to your browser (1)

- The browser then connects to the IP address of the server and downloads the web site. (1)
[Max 5]

points.criterion: A DNS server contains a list of domain names or corresponding IP addresses
The browser checks the local cached host file to check if it already holds the IP address
The local DNS server is queried for the IP address
If the local DNS server does not hold the IP address, the query is passed to another DNS server at a higher level until resolved
The address is passed on to DNS servers lower in the hierarchy
When the full address has been resolved, the IP address is passed to the browser
The browser connects to the IP address of the server and downloads the web site

scheme.model_answer: A DNS server contains lists of domain names and corresponding IP addresses. When a domain name is entered, the browser may check a local cached host file first. If needed, the local DNS server is queried for the IP address. If it does not have the address, the query is passed to higher-level DNS servers until the IP address is resolved, then the address is passed back down the hierarchy to the browser. The browser then connects to the server’s IP address and downloads the website.

parts.title: Networks, protocols and IP addressing (d)(i)
parts.text: Explain why FTP protocol is NOT suitable for live video streaming.

scheme.mark_scheme:
The file transfer protocol, breaks data into packets and can re-send lost or damaged packets … (1)
… it allows packets that have arrived in a random order to be reassembled … (1)
…which is not convenient for continuous data streaming (1)
[2]

points.criterion: FTP breaks data into packets and can re-send lost or damaged packets
FTP allows packets that arrived in random order to be reassembled
This is not convenient for continuous data streaming

scheme.model_answer: FTP can resend lost or damaged packets and reassemble packets that arrive in a random order. This is not convenient for continuous live video streaming because it can delay the stream.
scheme.ai_instructions: Award up to 2 marks from the listed points.

scheme.model_answer: FTP is convenient for transferring files between a client and a server over a network.
